title: Graceful hot-swap and tiered maintenance policy for dedicated nodes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets currently rely on disruptive node drains and blunt maintenance windows that cause transient throughput drops and increased tail latency for customers with strict throughput guarantees. Goal: Implement a graceful hot-swap flow and a tiered maintenance policy that preserves throughput SLAs during planned node maintenance and rolling upgrades. The feature should integrate with autoscaling and routing policies so that capacity reservations, prefilling, and staged connection drain prevent P50/P95 regressions during maintenance.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Nodes can be marked for tiered maintenance with a priority tag (critical, standard, background). 2) Critical-tier nodes must only be drained after capacity prefills or capacity reservations achieve target headroom for active shards. 3) Draining must support staged traffic eviction (streaming, long-poll, ephemeral sessions) and respect tokenized session TTLs to avoid abrupt cancellations. 4) Planner automatically triggers temporary autoscale up/down and pre-warm actions to keep per-tenant throughput >= configured guarantee during maintenance. 5) Console shows maintenance windows, affected shards, and a simulated throughput impact estimate. 6) Rollout can be rolled back per-fleet with no data loss and documented SLO for median/95th latency preserved within 10% of baseline.
implementation_notes: Design a maintenance controller that sits in the fleet orchestration plane and coordinates with: (a) Serving runtime to initiate soft drains (emit DRAIN_PREPARE, DRAIN_START, DRAIN_COMPLETE events), (b) Autoscaler API to request temporary capacity reservations or burst pools, (c) Smart routing to failover ongoing inflight requests to warm nodes, and (d) KV cache backfill to prepopulate hot prefixes on warmed nodes. The controller will use a state machine: PENDING -> PREFILLING -> SOFT_DRAIN -> HARD_DRAIN -> RETIRED. Prefill step uses historical seq-length distribution to decide prewarm tokens and cache keys. Implement new metrics: maintenance_headroom_pct, prefills_inflight, drained_sessions_count, estimated_throughput_impact. Add circuit breaker that aborts maintenance if estimated impact > configured risk threshold.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable in dedicated test fleets with synthetic workload that mirrors customer SLAs. Monitor maintenance_headroom_pct and P95 latency for 48h. Phase 2 (pilot): Opt-in customers with non-critical traffic and low scale. Phase 3: Default rollout for fleets configured with 'tiered-maintenance: enabled' with gradual ramp (5% fleets -> 25% -> 100%) and automatic rollback on SLO regression. Pre-reqs: autoscaler bump support and runtime kernel upgrade (see dependencies).
risks:
- Prefill misestimation could waste capacity and increase cost.
- Long-lived sessions may delay drain completion and block upgrades.
- Race between autoscaler decisions and drain controller might cause oscillation.
- Incorrect cache backfill ordering could increase tail latency post-swap.
